options.product: Microsoft Entra External ID - external tenant
options.plan: Basic MAU; upstream workforce entitlement unverified
options.region: No external or upstream tenant region selected; storage destinations not verified
options.configuration: Standard external tenant; Okta org OIDC code/client_secret_post; user-flow JIT; no SCIM add-on or Graph bridge

conditions: Select browser-delegated custom OIDC in a standard-mode external tenant, register its federation redirect URIs in an assigned Okta web app and attach the IdP to the application's sign-up/sign-in user flow; native authentication and workforce B2B guest invitation are outside this scope.

Choose the fixed Okta org issuer and discovery at https://developer.okta.com/docs/concepts/auth-servers/; this is not the /oauth2/default custom server, and its access tokens are not for the consuming SaaS API.

Use code and explicitly configure client_secret_post on both sides. Okta's default client_secret_basic is incompatible with the selected External ID interface; private_key_jwt must not be selected there even if displayed. See https://developer.okta.com/docs/api/openapi/okta-oauth/guides/client-auth .

This is an inferred protocol-compatible documentation candidate, not a vendor-certified or tested Okta connector. Issuer, metadata, claims and secret rotation need live validation; no client, account or integration was created.

The Basic MAU allowance at https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/pricing/details/microsoft-entra-external-id/ does not establish tenant or upstream entitlement, paid add-on access or a zero-cost guarantee.

evidence.summary: External ID documents configurable OIDC federation, with specific token-endpoint methods and code flow. Combining this with Okta's org OIDC and client-auth references proposes OPTIONAL for this exact scope; pair interoperability remains unverified.

conditions: Use the attached browser-delegated sign-up/sign-in user flow to create an external-tenant customer object at first federated sign-up; this is not pre-provisioning or workforce guest redemption.

Review issuer-bound sub and explicit claim/user-flow attribute mappings at https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/external-id/customers/reference-oidc-claims-mapping-customers . Email presence requires a truthful email_verified claim for creation; no constant true, email-only identity merge or automatic linking is asserted.
Email is required by default; the generic guide's optional-email setting is user-flow-wide. The selected Okta claims, account collision handling and repeat-login updates have not been tested.
First-sign-up object creation does not establish ongoing directory synchronization, group membership, deprovisioning or immediate revocation of application permissions, sessions or tokens.

evidence.summary: The external-tenant authentication overview describes creating a directory user during federated sign-up. This conditional first-sign-up proposal is not evidence of tested Okta identity correlation or continuing lifecycle synchronization.

conditions: The required direction is Okta workforce provisioning into the customer directory of this Basic external tenant, not outbound Entra application provisioning or OIDC sign-up.

The separate Entra SCIM server API needs P1 and an Azure-linked paid add-on; it is excluded here, and external-tenant applicability, Okta client interoperability and identity correlation remain unverified.

No paid add-on or Graph bridge is selected. UNKNOWN is not UNAVAILABLE; establish the inbound endpoint, entitlement, update/disable semantics and separate SaaS access/session enforcement before assigning availability.

evidence.summary: The billed Entra SCIM server guide does not establish an included Basic external-tenant provisioning path from Okta. OIDC federation and first-sign-up creation cannot fill this evidence gap.

conditions: External-tenant group administration, Graph membership edits and application roles do not establish Okta Group Push into this customer directory.
No Graph bridge is selected; native inbound group entitlement, stable identifiers, membership removals, nested-group behavior and deletions remain unverified for this pair.

OIDC group claims and JIT are not a SCIM Group lifecycle. Application-owned authorization and session/token revocation need independent evidence; UNKNOWN is not a claim that all group APIs are absent.

evidence.summary: The external-tenant table documents local user/group and role management, not native inbound Okta group lifecycle synchronization for this Basic scope.
